meta.source: GPM IMERG via NASA GIBS WMTS
meta.period: 25 complete calendar years, 2001-01-01 to 2025-12-31. 9124 daily composites (P1D) read, 25 years for every calendar month. The GIBS gap 2025-10-23 to 2025-10-29 has no published tile and is excluded.
meta.method: For every one of the 9124 days in the period the GIBS WMTS tile IMERG_Precipitation_Rate / GoogleMapsCompatible_Level6 / row 30 / col 53 was downloaded as a PNG. One tile covers all 300 pilot cells (lon 118.125 to 123.75 E, lat 5.616 to 11.178 N). The PNG was decoded with Pillow and each cell pixel was looked up in the GIBS colormap XML, which maps a colour to a precipitation-rate bin in mm per hour. The bin midpoint was taken as the value. The daily total in mm is that mean daily rate multiplied by 24. Verified against the half-hourly layer: on 2024-06-15 the daily tile read 0.19395 mm/hr and the mean of the 48 half-hourly tiles for the same pixel was 0.18771 mm/hr, so the daily composite is the 24 hour mean rate and the x24 conversion is correct. Daily totals were summed into monthly totals for each of the 25 years, then averaged across years to give one monthly climatological mean per cell in mm. annual_mm is the sum of the 12 monthly means.
meta.caveats: 1) IMERG native grid is 0.1 degrees, about 10 to 11 km. The GIBS Level 6 PNG is a regrid of that product onto a 256 x 256 pixel tile whose pixels are about 2.4 km at this latitude, so neighbouring pilot cells 2.23 km apart can share the same source value. The file is not an independent measurement per 2.23 km cell. 2) The GIBS colormap is quantised. Values below 0.1 mm/hr are the "Insignificant" class (rgb 191,191,191) and are read as 0, so a real daily total between 0 and 2.4 mm is lost. The smallest resolvable non-zero rate is 0.1 mm/hr, that is 2.4 mm per day. Dry month totals are therefore biased low by up to about 2.4 mm per rain day, which is at most a few tens of mm in a dry month. 3) GIBS publishes only one tile matrix level per layer in EPSG:3857. For this layer it is Level 6 only, so there is no finer GIBS tile to fall back on. 4) The colour for the top bin is rgb(58,3,48) with an open upper bound, so values above 53.0884 mm/hr are read as 53.09 mm/hr. No pilot cell reaches that. 5) Nodata pixels are rgb(128,128,128) and are reported as null for that cell-month. There were no nodata pixels at any of the 300 pilot cells in any of the 9124 tiles. 6) The period is 2001 to 2025, not the 1991 to 2020 window of the PAGASA station normals, because IMERG starts in June 2000. The 25 year window includes the very wet 2010 to 2012 period. An independent ERA5 climatology (Open-Meteo archive API, 1991 to 2020) at the same point gives 2,376.6 mm against 2,422.1 mm here, so the window and the product together account for about 2 percent. 7) This file replaces NASA POWER only as a rain climatology. It does not change the temperature, humidity, soil moisture or soil data in the pilot grid. 8) Across the 300 cells the annual total ranges from 2,255.9 to 2,558.9 mm with a standard deviation of 86.5 mm, so real rainfall varies by about 12 percent over the 30 by 40 km pilot area. The cell values are not a smooth field and neighbouring cells differ.

cross_checks.note: IMERG and ERA5 are independent 10 to 11 km products and they agree within 1.9 percent at Pagadian. The PAGASA Zamboanga City station, 55 to 100 km to the south west and in the rain shadow of the Zamboanga mountains, is the closest station with a full normals record and it is not representative of Pagadian. The PAGASA Cotabato City station, 110 km to the north east on the Sulu Sea coast, gives 2,414.3 mm, which is within 0.3 percent of the IMERG value for cell 6_9.

meta.colormap_note: The GIBS colormap for layer IMERG_Precipitation_Rate is GPM_Precipitation_Rate.xml, not IMERG_Precipitation_Rate.xml. The IMERG_Precipitation_Rate.xml URL returns HTTP 404. The correct file was read from the ows:Metadata element of the layer in the live WMTSCapabilities.xml.
meta.unit: GIBS layer unit is millimetres per hour (mm/hr) for the precipitation rate. Daily total in mm = mean daily rate x 24 h. monthly_mm and annual_mm are in mm.
meta.missing_tile_days: 2025-10-23 to 2025-10-29 (7 days, no tile published by GIBS)
meta.dry_month_definition: months_under_50mm counts calendar months whose climatological mean total is below 50 mm, the PAGASA dry-season monthly threshold used by the UbiMap model. longest_dry_spell_months is the longest run of consecutive calendar months under that same 50 mm threshold.
